key_insight: Sequential hot rotary swaging tailored Zr-4Nb-2Al microstructure and texture, trading compressive yield strength for greater plastic deformability and more uniform radial hardness.
engineering_relevance: Phase-field-controlled swaging offers a route to tune the strength–deformability balance of dual-phase zirconium rods.
method: Use electrical resistivity to select swaging temperatures: 880°C in β and 780°C in α+β.
Apply induction-assisted rotary swaging with thermographic temperature control, reducing rod diameter from 12 to 6.3 mm.
Evaluate microstructure, crystallographic texture, phase constitution, compression response, and radial hardness.
evidence_signal: At 72% total area reduction, prior-β grains refined to about 100 μm; subsequent α+β swaging lowered compressive yield strength from 1103 to 839 MPa, with maximum fracture strain reaching 32%.
watch_item: Reported compression results do not establish tensile, fatigue, or service-environment performance.
paper_title: Evolution of microstructure and crystallographic texture in a novel Zr-4Nb-2Al alloy during hot rotary swaging
